info.title: Doba Partner API
info.summary: Availability, rates and bookings for one hotel.
info.description:
The read-and-write interface a channel manager, a metasearch partner or
the hotel's own tooling integrates against.

Three rules run through the whole of it:

- **Money is integer minor units plus a currency**, never a decimal
  string. `{"amount": 12500, "currency": "EUR"}` is 125.00 EUR, and a
  partner cannot lose a cent parsing it as a float.
- **A date is a date.** `check_in` is `2026-09-07`, not a timestamp in
  somebody's timezone. Only genuine instants (`created_at`,
  `hold_expires_at`) are RFC 3339.
- **Nothing here decides whether a room is free.** Every endpoint calls
  the same services the hotel's own website does, so the API and the
  website can never disagree about a night.

Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. Integrate against
`type` — those URIs are part of the contract and will not change. The
`title` is for a human reading a log and may be reworded at any time.

tags.name: Hotel
tags.description: What this property is and what it sells.

tags.name: Availability
tags.description: What is free, at what price, and pushing that back.

get.description:
Discovery. A partner calls this once at setup to learn the
currency, the locales and the booking window it must respect.

Only active types, in the hotel's own display order. `code` is the
identifier every other endpoint takes — names are translated and
change, codes do not.

The raw calendar, night by night. `available` already has holds
deducted — it is what a new booking could actually take, not the
allotment.

Nights the hotel has never opened simply do not appear. An absent
night is not a bookable one.

parameters.name: room_type
parameters.description: Restrict to one room type code.

put.description:
An **idempotent range write**, which is why it is `PUT`. Sending
the identical body twice changes nothing the first call did not —
these are not increments, and a partner whose push timed out can
simply send it again.

`weekdays` is a bitmask (Monday = 1, Tuesday = 2 … Sunday = 64),
so "Saturdays in July, minimum stay three" is one entry rather
than five.

Nights where the requested allotment is below what is already sold
and held are **refused individually** and returned in `refused`.
The rest of the push still applies: one oversold night in a six
month range should not throw the range away.

Idempotent range write, as with availability. Prices are minor
units.

A price cannot be pushed per rate plan. In Doba a rate plan is an
adjustment off the room's price rather than an independent price,
so a per-plan push would be stored and never read — sending
`rate_plan` is refused with `rate-plan-not-pushable` rather than
silently ignored.

422.description: Invalid, or a per-plan price was pushed.

get.summary: Bookable stays for a set of dates
get.description:
The same search the website's own funnel runs — minimum stay,
closed-to-arrival, closures and occupancy limits all applied. A
room type that appears here is bookable for these exact dates.

200.description: Bookable offers. An empty `data` means sold out, not an error.

get.description:
The pull endpoint a channel manager polls. Page with `next_cursor`
until it is `null`.

Cursor rather than offset on purpose: offset pagination over a
table that is being written to while you page through it skips
rows and repeats others, and a partner loses bookings without ever
seeing an error.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Only bookings changed at or after this instant.

post.description:
Goes through the same service, the same row locks and the same
restriction checks as the website's own checkout.

**`Idempotency-Key` is required.** A partner whose request times
out will retry, and an endpoint that cannot tell a retry from a
second booking sells the room twice. Retrying with the same key
replays the original response byte for byte and carries
`Idempotent-Replay: true`. Reusing a key with a *different* body
is a bug in the caller and is refused with
`idempotency-key-reused` rather than hidden behind a replay.

The booking is created `pending` and holds inventory until
`hold_expires_at`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique per booking attempt, reused verbatim on retry.

201.description: Booked, or a replay of the original response.

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present and `true` when this is a replay rather than a new booking.

409.description:
`no-availability` — the stay went while the partner was
deciding; the first unavailable night is in `date`.
`idempotency-key-reused` — same key, different body.

post.description:
`refund` is computed from the cancellation policy **snapshotted on
the booking when it was taken**, never from today's rate plan: the
guest is owed what they agreed to, even if the hotel has since
changed its terms.

`paid` comes back alongside it because a refund is capped at what
was actually taken — a bare `0` on a booking that was never
charged reads like a forfeited stay.

A booking that has already been cancelled, or that the guest has
checked out of, is refused with `not-cancellable`.

409.description: `not-cancellable` — this booking is past the point of cancelling.

get.description:
Scoped to the calling key: a partner sees only the endpoints it
registered, never another partner's URL.

post.description:
Returns a signing secret **once**. It is not readable afterwards;
an endpoint whose secret is lost has to be replaced.

Every delivery carries `X-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, where the
hex is `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")`. The timestamp is
inside the signed string, so a delivery captured and replayed
hours later fails verification even though the body is identical —
reject anything with a `t` older than your tolerance.

Deliveries are **at least once and may arrive out of order**.
Dedupe on `event_id`, and ignore an event whose `updated_at` is
older than what you have already stored, or you will eventually
resurrect a cancelled booking. An endpoint that fails 20 times
running is disabled.

url.description:
`https` only. A payload carries guest names and stay
dates, and signing it does not stop anyone reading it.

201.description: Subscribed. The only time `secret` is ever returned.

post.description:
Queues a real, really-signed `webhook.test` delivery, so a partner
can prove their signature check works before a booking depends on
it. `202`, because the delivery is queued rather than sent inline.

ApiKeyId.name: X-Api-Key-Id
ApiKeyId.description: The public half of the key pair, `dk_…`.

ApiSecret.name: X-Api-Secret
ApiSecret.description:
The secret half, shown once when the key is issued and stored
hashed. There is no recovery path on purpose: a key the admin can
read back is a key that leaks with a database backup.

BookingReference.name: reference
BookingReference.description: The booking reference, as returned when it was taken.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing, unknown, revoked or expired credentials. Deliberately
identical whether the key id is unknown or the secret is wrong:
telling a caller which half they got right is an oracle for
guessing the other.

Forbidden.description:
The key is valid but lacks the scope for this route, or is calling
from an address outside its allowlist. Distinct from `401` on
purpose — a partner whose egress address changed needs to know
that, not rotate a key that was fine.

ValidationFailed.description: The request is not valid; `errors` is keyed by field.

Money.description:
Integer minor units and an ISO 4217 code. `{"amount": 12500,
"currency": "EUR"}` is 125.00 EUR. Never a decimal string, so a
partner cannot parse it as a float, multiply it by three nights
and book a stay for 374.99999999.

Problem.description:
RFC 9457. Branch on `type` — those URIs are the contract. `title`
is for a human reading a log and may be reworded at any time.

errors.description: Field name to messages. Present on `validation-failed`.

date.description: The first unavailable night. Present on `no-availability`.

address.description: Keys the hotel has not filled in are absent.

booking_window_days.description: How far ahead a stay may be booked.

hold_minutes.description: How long an unconfirmed booking holds its inventory.

code.description: The stable identifier. Names are translated, codes are not.

available.description: Units a new booking could take. Holds already deducted.

closed_to_arrival.description: A stay may span this night but not begin on it.

closed_to_departure.description: A stay may span this night but not end on it.

AvailabilityUpdate.description: Fields left out are left alone.

price.description: Minor units, like every other amount here.

rate_plan.description:
Refused with `rate-plan-not-pushable`. Documented so the
refusal is not a surprise: a plan is an adjustment off the
room price, so a per-plan price would be stored and never
read.

WeekdayMask.description:
Bitmask. Monday 1, Tuesday 2, Wednesday 4, Thursday 8, Friday 16,
Saturday 32, Sunday 64. Weekends are 96; every day, 127, is the
default.

refused.description:
Nights left untouched because the requested allotment was
below what is already sold and held. The rest of the push
still applied.

total.description: The whole stay on the default plan, not one night.

cancellation_hours.description: Free cancellation up to this many hours before arrival.

notes.description: The guest's own request, shown to the front desk.

refund.description: From the policy snapshotted on the booking, not today's.

paid.description: What was actually taken. A refund cannot exceed it.

source.description:
Where it came from — `direct`, `api`, `ical`, or a channel's
own name. Not an enum: connecting a new channel must not be a
breaking change.

refundable.description: Snapshotted when booked, not read from today's plan.

hold_expires_at.description:
When a `pending` booking stops holding its inventory. `null`
once confirmed — a hold is not a booking, and a partner needs
to know exactly how long it has.

updated_at.description:
Deliveries can arrive out of order. Ignore an event older than
what you have stored, or you will resurrect a cancelled
booking.

active.description: Set false automatically after 20 consecutive failures.
